Subject: EU/APAC region split & failover plan - Renewal SOW

Hi Oliver —

Thanks again for the renewal conversation last week. Per our call, attached is draft SOW v3 that outlines the proposed region topology for EU primary (Frankfurt) with APAC (Singapore) as a warm standby and automated failover path. Key items in this version:

- Data residency: customer traffic and persistent storage for EU tenants will remain in EU nodes. APAC will act as stateless warm standby; logs & audit trail replication is limited to hashed metadata (no PII replication without customer opt-in).
- Failover behavior: automated routing to APAC if EU latched nodes breach 95% capacity or in the event of a region-level outage. Traffic will be replay-protected via request deduplication TTL.
- Capacity uplift during renewal: suggested commit +25% vCPU/GPU capacity for Q4 ramp.
- Pricing: we included a timebound Q4 discount and optional burst credits for APAC during cutover.

Attachments: BH_SOW_v3.pdf (SOW), eu-apac-failover-diagram.png (topology sketch).

Action items for this thread:
1) Can procurement confirm whether blueharbor requires APAC data residency for a subset of customers?
2) Can ops confirm latency SLAs for the EU primary (target p95 < 120ms for inference)?

If useful, Karthik and Marcus are looping in below for tech details. Happy to jump on a 30m to walk through the diagram.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Account Exec, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Thanks, Naomi / Oliver. Quick technical notes: 

- APAC residency subset: if Blue Harbor requires APAC-only tenancy for a subset of customers we can provision dedicated APAC tenant pools (separate tenancy) — that is a heavier lift (requires separate data egress policy and KMS partition) and would be priced as an add-on.
- Warm standby timeline: baseline provisioning (network, VM images, container registry sync) ~2 weeks after SOW sign + config & smoke testing 2 more weeks. So conservative ETA: 4 weeks to warm standby availability.
- Failover safeguards: we will enable prefix KV caching and request de-duplication to prevent double-processing on failover; any persisted customer data remains only in region of record unless you opt into cross-region archival.
- Latency: EU p95 target of <120ms is reachable for your median payloads; we'll need sample payloads to run a short perf test.

Attachment: redwood-geo-terms-diff.docx — a one-page summary of what changes in terms when adding APAC tenancy.

If procurement needs language for the DPA clause, Marcus can suggest the specific wording.

Oliver / team —

Appended a slightly more detailed ops diagram and a short runbook for the failover path (attached). Highlights: 

- Warm standby behavior: APAC nodes will pull model artifacts and maintain KV cache skeletons; no customer PII stored in APAC until explicit cross-region archival is enabled.
- Failover detection: we use multi-signal detection (routing gateway health + node CPU/GPU saturation + redis cluster reachability) with a 90s decision window before traffic shift.
- Cutover testing: recommend two staged cutovers during a low-traffic window + one scripted failback test.
- Capacity uplift: during the first 3 months after renewal we suggest an autoscale policy of +40% burst capacity for APAC to absorb test traffic and warm caches. This is refundable as burst credits if not consumed.

Next steps from ops side:
1) I'll schedule a 45-minute ops walkthrough with your infra team (Oliver / Hannah) the week after SOW sign.
2) We will provide a short payload bucket (5 sample requests) and can run perf tests ahead of sign to validate p95.

Attachments: eu-apac-failover-diagram.png (updated), failover-runbook.txt (text).

Regards,
